(34) H_TFI = − Σ_<i,j> σz_i σz_j − g Σ_i σx_i with 'Pauli matrices', on 'a two-dimensional square lattice of side length Lx = Ly ... with open boundary conditions' (Sec. 5): QMBL's TFIsing with h = g, open on all four sides; Table 2 prints total energies of the '4×4 TFI model' (−57.8 for 16 sites). What the reference is (brief question 5): 'reference eigenvalues E_α,ref for the TFI model (34) were computed using the block MPS alternating optimization algorithm described in [23]' ([23] = Dolgov, Khoromskij, Oseledets & Savostyanov, Comput. Phys. Commun. 185, 1207 (2014)); 'With a maximum bond dimension of 5000, reference energies for the TFI model were obtained with relative accuracy of order 10−6 for Lx ≤ 8'. It is a variational MPS energy, not an exact reference; on 4 x 4 the bond dimension cap 5000 exceeds the largest Schmidt rank 2^8 = 256, so the MPS can represent the state exactly. Against QMBL's ED (-26.86050463952785): printed − ED = -4.72e-10, i.e. the printed value lies 4.7e-10 below exact, inside its eighth-decimal rounding (tolerance 5e-9); not a bound violation. bound_type variational is right; peer_reviewed false (v1 only). The α = 1 cells are excited states, not rows. Not a duplicate of the exact row (different source and computation). Record row (best variational).
